# E01: deterministic reliability aggregation

## Scope

Extend the existing Agent Dev benefit report and scenario registry. Do not introduce a metrics platform, change product defaults, product locks, approval semantics, or add scheduled automation.

## Acceptance contract

- Pre-register `k=3`, `minCases=20`, and the flake threshold in `shared/agent-dev/reliability-fixture.json`.
- Report `pass^k` (all k trials pass) separately from `pass@k` (at least one trial passes).
- A case with missing, timeout, crash, or skip trial is incomplete. Exclude it from both metric denominators, retain it in the report, and preserve its reason.
- Flake is first trial failure followed by a fixed rerun success. A successful retry does not erase the original first failure. Safety-critical checks require zero skip and zero flake.
- Positive anchors must pass every trial. Negative anchors must reject every trial. Any violation fails the gate.
- Fewer than 20 complete cases at k=3 yields `insufficient-sample`, never PASS.
- Include raw denominator, both reliability metrics, flake, incomplete details, gate, and reasons.
- The fixture is explicitly a deterministic oracle. It must not be described as real-provider, human, or generalization evidence.

## Fast gate

Run the targeted unit tests, runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, and harness validate/dry-run. Verify credential scanning has zero hits and SHA256SUMS can be read back. The four-language README review is recorded as no-change because this is an internal report-only change.

# Reliability aggregation boundary

The reliability aggregator is a pure deterministic data transformation. It must not call providers, start processes, read tests at runtime, perform network requests, or alter product behavior.

`pass^k` means the proportion of complete cases for which all `k` trials pass. `pass@k` means the proportion of complete cases with at least one passing trial; these names and numerators must never be conflated. Cases with missing, timeout, crash, or skip are incomplete, excluded from the metric denominator, and explicitly retained in the report.

Flake means first trial failure and later fixed rerun success. It is reported, not used to erase the original failure. Positive anchors require every trial to pass and negative anchors require every trial to reject. Anchor violations fail the gate. An insufficient complete sample is `insufficient-sample` and cannot be promoted to PASS.

The fixture is a deterministic oracle, not a claim about real model, provider, human, or generalization performance. The aggregation is internal reporting only and does not change product defaults, locks, approval semantics, dependencies, or automation schedules.

# E01 reliability aggregation acceptance record

## Result

The Agent Dev benefit report now consumes the pre-registered deterministic reliability fixture and emits a dedicated reliability section. It reports the raw case denominator, complete-case denominator, `pass^k`, `pass@k`, flake rate, missing/timeout/crash/skip counts, anchor checks, gate, and gate reasons. Incomplete cases are retained in the report but excluded from reliability denominators.

`pass^k` and `pass@k` are separate metrics. A positive anchor must pass all trials and a negative anchor must reject all trials; violations fail the gate. The default fixture is `k=3`, requires at least 20 complete cases, and therefore reports `insufficient-sample` while the fixture contains incomplete cases. The flake threshold is pre-registered in the fixture.

The fixture is explicitly marked as a deterministic oracle. This record makes no claim about real providers, humans, model generalization, or production behavior.

## Boundary review

This change is limited to the internal evaluation report and deterministic aggregation library. It does not change product defaults, product locks, approval semantics, dependencies, user-visible interfaces, or schedules. The README does not require a change because no user-visible interface or configuration changed.

## Fast-gate record

The acceptance record requires the scoped unit/type/lint checks, harness validate and dry-run, zero-hit credential scan, and readable SHA256SUMS to be verified by the owning release process. No runtime test discovery, provider call, network request, or process side effect is part of the aggregator implementation.
